not. I think one of the biggest factors is going to be clarity. This is one of the bizarre parts of the market which is when
the market starts believing something negative is around the corner it starts to make some assumptions about what earnings
can do in the future how much lower they can go in the future. And historically the unknown is worse than the known. And so
we see this phenomenon of companies that trade down going into an earnings print. And then when they actually report the
negative guidance and sometimes that guidance is worse than what some of the whisper is. We'll see those stocks trade up.
So the unknown here is what is the scope of the build out of AI going to look like over the next one to three years. And of course

that's so important and central to the conversation is that that topic how big the brain of AI the hardware part of AI is not only
impacts companies who provide technology to that build out but also as that brain gets bigger it's the platform that AI
applications can be built on. And so there's another wave other waves whether it be personalized agents or whether it's
physically I think it built on top of that. So this is kind of the key piece is understanding what effectively the build out is
